facts.text: Most snowflakes have six sides or arms, and it is very unlikely that any two are exactly alike.
Reindeer eyes change colour: golden in summer and deep blue in winter.
Candy canes were once plain white sticks. The red stripes came later.
A real Christmas tree takes seven to ten years to grow.
Long ago, people hung apples and nuts on their Christmas trees.
In Norway, people hide their brooms on Christmas Eve so witches can't borrow them!
In Czechia, people cut a cherry branch on 4 December and put it in water. If it blooms by Christmas, it brings luck!
Jingle Bells was the first song played in space! In 1965 two astronauts played it on a tiny harmonica and little bells.
A snowflake can take up to an hour to fall from the clouds to your nose.
Polar bears have black skin under their fluffy fur.
In Iceland, thirteen Yule Lads visit one by one before Christmas. One of them loves to slam doors!
Gingerbread houses are famous from the fairy tale Hansel and Gretel.
In Japan, a fluffy cake with strawberries is the favourite Christmas treat.
Both male and female reindeer can grow antlers.

activities.text: Draw a picture of your dream snowman. What is he wearing?
Fold a piece of paper, snip some shapes and unfold your very own snowflake.
Sing your favourite Christmas song as loud as you can. Then as quietly as you can!
Help a grown-up in the kitchen today. Stirring, sprinkling and tasting all count!
Make a paper chain with one link for every sleep left until Christmas.
Build a blanket fort and read a story inside it with a torch.
Go on a treasure hunt around your home and count every Christmas star, bell and tree you can find.
Make a Christmas card for someone who isn't expecting one.
Dance like a reindeer for one whole song. No giggling allowed!
Hide a tiny toy somewhere in the room and let your family hunt for it.
Put on your warmest socks and have a cosy family movie night.
Stick paper stars on your window to light the way for {bringer}.
Tell your family the silliest Christmas story you can make up.
Fill a jar with little notes about what you love about your family.

kindness.text: Give someone in your family a really big hug today.
With a grown-up, pick a toy you've outgrown and set it aside for a child who'd love it.
Help tidy up without anybody asking. Watch their faces!
Tell someone something you really like about them.
Put a little seed or oats on the windowsill or in the garden for the winter birds.
Make someone laugh today. Your best joke, please!
Say a big thank you to someone who looks after you.
Let someone else go first today, and smile while you do it.
